Child Won't Use the Arm: Reduce or Image?

A pull with a normal elbow is reduced; anything else is imaged

DiagnosisManagementPractice
Bottom line

A pull on the arm at 1 to 4 years, an arm held extended and pronated, and no swelling, deformity or bony point tenderness: radial head subluxation (nursemaid's elbow). Reduce without imaging.

Reduce:

  • Hyperpronation (more first-attempt success), or supination with flexion
  • Uses the arm within minutes (most by 10, 90% by 30): done; no radiograph or sling; counsel against pulling the arm

Image first with swelling, deformity or point tenderness, a fall rather than a pull, or age over 5; image if the arm stays unused after reduction.

An exam line describing the maneuver and a child reaching for toys afterward is the treatment already done: nothing further.

A mechanism that does not fit, no mechanism at all, or a fracture before walking: suspect abuse; skeletal survey under 2 years, and report.

Diagnosis
Defining findings Nursemaid's elbow – axial traction on an extended, pronated arm slips the annular ligament over the radial head · Exam – arm extended and pronated; no swelling, bruising, deformity or bony point tenderness · Supracondylar fracture – fall on an outstretched hand (extension type); swelling; posterior fat pad sign
Management and treatment
Management ladder: the unused arm
TierInterventionEscalate when
ReduceHyperpronation or supination with flexionArm still unused after reduction attempts
ImageElbow radiographsFracture, or a normal film with the arm still unused
ReferImmobilize; orthopedicsTop rung
By situation Recurrence – about 1 in 5; counsel against pulling the arm · Displaced supracondylar – closed reduction and pinning; a pale, pulseless hand is urgent
Practice
  1. 3-year-old girl who will not use her left arm pulled up by the wrist as she stumbled holds the arm extended and pronated at her side No swelling, bruising or deformity; no bony point tenderness Afebrile → Radial head subluxation → a pull on an extended, pronated arm at 1 to 4 years, with no swelling, deformity or point tenderness: a clinical diagnosis; reduce without imaging
  2. 3-year-old girl not using her right arm after being swung by her hands no swelling, deformity or point tenderness her elbow was supinated and flexed 15 minutes later she reaches for toys with that arm Afebrile → No further intervention → the maneuver was the treatment, and using the arm confirms the reduction: no radiograph or sling; counsel against pulling the arm
  3. 6-year-old boy who fell off monkey bars onto his outstretched hand elbow swollen and tender above the joint will not bend or straighten it Fingers warm; radial pulse present Afebrile · lateral radiograph: posterior fat pad sign → Supracondylar fracture → a fall on an outstretched hand with elbow swelling and a posterior fat pad: supracondylar fracture; check the anterior interosseous nerve and the brachial artery
  4. 6-year-old boy with a displaced supracondylar fracture of the right humerus right hand cool and pale no palpable radial pulse Makes an OK sign; forearm compartments soft T 37.0 °C · capillary refill 5 seconds → Brachial artery injury → a pale, cool, pulseless hand after a supracondylar fracture is brachial artery injury: urgent orthopedic reduction and vascular assessment; the intact OK sign spares the anterior interosseous nerve
  5. 3-year-old girl with her second pulled elbow this year, reduced today both times her brother lifted her by one hand using the arm normally within minutes Growth and development normal; no bruises or other injuries Afebrile → Counsel the family to avoid pulling the arm → recurrence is common (about 1 in 5) until the ligament strengthens after age 5; a fitting mechanism in a well child needs counseling, not an abuse workup
  6. 10-month-old boy who will not move his left arm mother says he rolled off the sofa yesterday not yet crawling; no prior fractures Bruise on the left upper arm; white sclerae Afebrile · radiograph: spiral fracture of the humeral shaft → Non-accidental trauma → a spiral fracture in a child who cannot generate the twist, a delay in care and a history that does not fit: suspected abuse; skeletal survey (under 2 years) and report; white sclerae make osteogenesis imperfecta less likely
  7. 2-year-old girl not using her arm after her mother pulled her from a puddle arm held extended and pronated; no swelling two reduction attempts, no click Still not reaching 30 minutes later Afebrile · no bony point tenderness → Radiographs of the elbow → most children use the arm within 10 minutes and 90% by 30; still not using it after reduction attempts: radiographs for an occult fracture, and if normal, immobilize and refer to orthopedics
Pairs with Suspected Child Abuse: Fractures and the Next Step: corner, rib and multiple healing fractures. Brachial Plexus Injury at Birth: the newborn who does not move an arm.
Transferable rule

Read the exam section for the treatment already given, and image only when the mechanism or the elbow says fracture.
